interest: Shows SCAP-FEC friction over labor-union political rights in early occupation Japan, plus chaotic State Department inter-agency routing.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file contains State Department records from September to November 1946 concerning the formation, legal protection, and regulation of Japanese trade unions and workers' organizations under the Allied Occupation. The collection begins with Despatch No. 601 from the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan (Tokyo), transmitting the First Interim Report by SCAP's General Headquarters, which summarizes post-surrender labor policies, the abrogation of repressive laws, collective bargaining rights, and statistical data on burgeoning union membership across Japan. The remainder of the file documents internal State Department deliberations and bureaucratic friction surrounding the revision of Far Eastern Commission paper FEC-SC-032 (C4-009/8, 'Principles for Japanese Trade Unions') and its alignment with policy directive SWNCC 92/1. These memoranda and notes reveal inter-agency coordination efforts among the State, War, Navy, and Labor Departments, addressing controversies such as SCAP's objections to unions engaging in political activities and national political reconstruction, while resolving internal confusion within the office of Assistant Secretary John H. Hilldring over diplomatic clearance and voting instructions.

subfiles.about: A State Department routing slip concerning the circulation of Despatch No. 601 from Tokyo and the retention of its enclosed SCAP labor report by the Reference collection.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip tracks Despatch No. 601's circulation in November 1946; REF is told to retain the enclosed SCAP report.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip for Despatch No. 601
subfiles.to: Chis, Agr, Eo. Pat, Nat. Pat, Trans, Trade, REF

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch forwarding and summarizing SCAP's First Interim Report on the development and treatment of Japanese labor organizations since the surrender.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan (drafted by Glenn A. Abbey)
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 601 transmits SCAP's first interim report on labor directives since the surrender: eleven principles including union rights, collective bargaining, dissolving ultranationalist labor fronts, and limiting strikes only for military security, with union membership data by industry and prefecture.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 601 from USPOLAD Tokyo: Transmission of First Interim Report on Treatment of Workers' Organizations in Japan Since the Surrender

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum transmitting the latest revision of Far Eastern Commission paper FEC-SC-032 (C4-009/8) regarding principles for Japanese trade unions.
subfiles.from: Mr. Stone (OIC - Office of International Information and Cultural Affairs / drafted by Gordon G. Bowles)
subfiles.summary: Stone sends Hilldring the revised FEC-SC-032 draft ('Principles for Japanese Trade Unions') from SWNCC 92/1, noting near-unanimous Committee agreement, and recommends clearing it within the U.S. government before FEC approval.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Stone to Hilldring on Revision of FEC-SC-032 (Principles for Japanese Trade Unions)
subfiles.to: Major General John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)

subfiles.about: A detailed sixteen-point comparison between the U.S. policy document SWNCC 92/1 and the Far Eastern Commission draft C4-009/8 on Japanese trade union principles.
subfiles.from: Gordon G. Bowles (ADO / Committee No. 4 U.S. Representative)
subfiles.summary: Analysis compares FEC draft C4-009/8 with SWNCC 92/1 on postwar Japanese labor policy, noting SCAP objected to language on unions' political participation and party support, and reviewing provisions on adult education, union federations, anti-espionage and strikebreaking bans, and excluding totalitarian organizations.
subfiles.title: Comparison of SWNCC 92/1 ('Treatment of Japanese Workers' Organizations') with FEC Paper C4-009/8 ('Principles for Japanese Trade Unions')

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum reporting conversations with Stout and Bowles and advising that the FEC trade union paper be filed without further action.
subfiles.summary: Memo tells Cameron that Bowles had already secured Gross's concurrence before Committee No. 4, so no further action is needed on the FEC trade union paper; recommends simply filing it.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to Cameron Recommending No Further Action on FEC Trade Union Paper
subfiles.to: Ward M. Cameron (Assistant to Assistant Secretary Hilldring)

subfiles.about: A brief handwritten office memorandum requesting a telephone call regarding the trade union policy file.
subfiles.summary: Office note: S. L. Lane asks Joe O'Sullivan to call about the FEC trade union paper matter.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from S. L. Lane to Joe O'Sullivan

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum directing Stout to coordinate the FEC trade union paper within the government and obtain General Hilldring's approval.
subfiles.from: Ward M. Cameron (Assistant to Assistant Secretary Hilldring)
subfiles.summary: Cameron tells Stout the FEC trade union paper needs an official U.S. position before Committee No. 4's vote, and asks him to coordinate agencies and secure Hilldring's approval.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Cameron to Stout Requesting Coordination of FEC Trade Union Paper

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum instructing O'Sullivan to urgently review the FEC trade union paper during Stout's absence and prepare recommendations for General Hilldring.
subfiles.from: Ward M. Cameron (Assistant to Assistant Secretary Hilldring)
subfiles.summary: Cameron urges O'Sullivan, covering for Stout, to review the FEC trade union paper immediately, since Gross's clearance assumed by Stout was never actually given, and report recommendations to Hilldring.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Cameron to O'Sullivan Assigning Urgent Review of FEC Trade Union Paper

subfiles.about: A brief memorandum inquiring whether the FEC trade union policy paper had actually been reviewed and cleared by Gross.
subfiles.summary: Cameron asks Gross to confirm Stout's claim that the trade union matter was already handled, so the file can be returned to Stone with a confirming note.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Cameron to Gross Inquiring About Clearance of FEC Paper

subfiles.about: A handwritten memorandum from Gross explaining that he discussed the paper by telephone with Bowles but had not formally cleared it.
subfiles.summary: Gross tells Cameron he only discussed a point or two by phone with Bowles and never cleared the full trade union paper; Stout should read it and make formal recommendations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Gross to Cameron Clarifying Status of Clearance with Bowles

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum reporting that Bowles had already discussed the trade union paper with Gross and Committee No. 4, obviating the need for further State Department action.
subfiles.summary: Stout tells Cameron that Bowles had already conferred with Gross and attended an FEC Committee 4 session, and War, Navy, and Labor had commented, so no further action is needed absent a new request.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Stout to Cameron Regarding FEC Committee 4 Action on Trade Union Paper
